test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

You can have accused / me of being lazy, / but I will not finish / the project right now.
solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 3: You can have accused".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"You can have accused" **is a grammatical **error**. The **correct **phrase should be **"You can accuse".**
 
• The use of **"can have accused"** is inappropriate. "**Can**" is a **modal **verb and is typically followed by the **base form of the verb** which is "**accuse**".
 
• The corrected part of the sentence "You can accuse me of being lazy" suggests the speaker is open to the accusation of being lazy.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is: *"**You can accuse** me of being lazy, but I will not finish the project right now."* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The verb '**accused**' takes **'of'** as a preposition after it. "**accused **me **of**".
 
• **Accused (अभियुक्त)** - A person or group of people who are charged with or on trial for a crime.
 
 
• **Example:** The woman **accused **her neighbour **of **stealing her mail.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__

 
• **1.** "You **can **accuse me of being lazy, but I will not finish the project right now."

 
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct and makes sense.
 
 
 
• **2.** "You **have **accused me of being lazy, but I will not finish the project right now."
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct but **contextually does not make clear sense.**
